messages:
liam: FYI seeing a new p99 tail during the late-afternoon spike on canary. p50=28ms p95=74ms p99=420ms, CPU on nodes looks fine but KV cache miss rate jumped from 3%->22% under 1200 concurrent streams.
anya: ugh, sounds like contention on the KV hotset + batching interactions. Any change to microbatch sizing or kernel rollouts recently? :eyes:
liam: we rolled kernel-selector v2 last night (prefer fast-gemm for small seqs). microbatch target was auto (observed batching around 16). No deliberate change to KV TTL.
infra-bot: [alert] infra/kv-cache-high-miss rate on pool-gpu-2 (alert_id: alert-2026-17900023)
ben: did you profile an example run? flamegraphs or pprof would help. Also need to correlate per-request kv_hit/miss labels with queue time.
liam: attached quick profile (ran locally against canary with 1k concurrent sessions):
```
pprof -http=localhost:6060 cpu.prof
# observed long tail inside kv_lookup() when eviction scanned >500 entries
```
maria: did an A/B this morning toggling microbatch_limit: 8 vs 4 under 1k concurrency. Results: mb=8 => throughput +12% but p99 +2.3x; mb=4 => throughput -9% but p99 ~120ms stable. KV miss rate tracks with mb size since larger MB increases simultaneous distinct prefixes hitting cache.
anya: interesting — so microbatch sizing is trading off unit throughput vs tail-latency because of increased working set. We should consider adaptive mb that shrinks when kv_miss_rate > 10%.
ben: agree. Also kernel selection might amplify the problem: fast-gemm reduces per-op latency but increases parallel memory footprint per model instance, exacerbating KV pressure. We saw similar with matmul_tiling change earlier.
liam: experiment idea: add a fast path that switches to conservative batching+kernel when kv_miss_rate spikes, then fallback after cooldown. Something like: if kv_miss_rate > 0.1 && qlen>50 => set mb_target=4 and kernel=memory-saver.
devops: here's a quick config snippet we tested in staging that does adaptive mb based on a simple threshold:
```
routing:
  adaptive_batching:
    enabled: true
    thresholds:
      kv_miss_rate: 0.10
      queue_len: 50
    actions:
      set_mb_target: 4
      set_kernel: memory-saver
    cooldown_s: 30
```
maria: ran that config for 30m with 1.2k concurrency. p99 dropped from 420ms->140ms, throughput dropped 8% but overall SLO improved. KV eviction scans per miss dropped by ~60%.
anya: great. For longer-term: consider making eviction cheaper (LRU buckets, incremental eviction) and exposing per-tenant kv_reservation to prevent noisy-neighbor blowups. Also add a kernel memory-footprint signal to kernel-selector heuristics.
liam: action items: 1) ben to add kernel mem-footprint metric to selector (ETA 2d), 2) devops to roll adaptive config to canary (ETA today), 3) maria to run extended soak with mixed seq lengths (ETA 24h). I'll monitor p99 and kv_miss dashboards and post back.
ben: I’ll also throw together a small sim that models working-set growth vs mb size to pick the optimal thresholds.
devops: rolling adaptive config to canary now. infra-bot will report any regressions. :rocket:
infra-bot: [notice] rollout started for adaptive-batching config on canary pool (deploy-1790002345-adaptive-1).
liam: thanks team — will update thread with soak numbers. If anyone wants the raw pprof or perf traces ping me and I’ll drop them here.
